name: Barclays

summary.text: Barclays PLC is a British bank. On this site it appears through the 2009 sale of Barclays Global Investors to BlackRock. Its 2008 capital raisings from Qatari investors produced the UK's first criminal trial of bank executives over financial-crisis conduct: in June 2017 the Serious Fraud Office charged Barclays PLC and four former executives with conspiracy to commit fraud, and in February 2018 charged Barclays Bank PLC with unlawful financial assistance over a $3 billion loan to Qatar Holding LLC. The corporate charges were dismissed by the Crown Court in May 2018, John Varley was acquitted after the Court of Appeal upheld a ruling of insufficient evidence in June 2019, and Roger Jenkins, Thomas Kalaris and Richard Boath were acquitted on 28 February 2020. On 25 November 2024 the Financial Conduct Authority fined Barclays £40 million for recklessly failing to disclose fees paid to the Qatari investors.

facts.claim: On 20 June 2017 the Serious Fraud Office charged Barclays PLC and former executives John Varley, Roger Jenkins, Thomas Kalaris and Richard Boath with conspiracy to commit fraud by false representation in relation to the June 2008 capital raising, with further charges relating to the October 2008 capital raising and a $3 billion loan to Qatar in November 2008.
facts.quote: Conspiracy to commit fraud by false representation was charged over the June 2008 raising against Barclays Plc, John Varley, Roger Jenkins, Thomas Kalaris and Richard Boath

sources.title: SFO charges in Barclays Qatar capital raising case

facts.claim: In February 2018 the SFO charged Barclays Bank PLC with unlawful financial assistance relating to a US$3 billion loan to Qatar Holding LLC between 1 October and 30 November 2008.
facts.quote: charged Barclays Bank Plc with unlawful financial assistance, relating to a US$3 billion loan given to Qatar Holding LLC between 1 October and 30 November 2008

sources.title: Further SFO charges in Barclays Qatar capital raising case

facts.claim: The charges against Barclays PLC and Barclays Bank PLC were dismissed by the Crown Court in May 2018; the High Court rejected the SFO's application to reinstate them and refused permission to appeal to the Supreme Court.
facts.quote: Charges against Barclays Plc and Barclays Bank Plc over the 2008 capital raisings were dismissed by the Crown Court in May 2018.

sources.title: Barclays PLC and Qatar Holding LLC (case page)

facts.claim: On 28 February 2020 Roger Jenkins, Richard Boath and Thomas Kalaris were acquitted of fraud in what the SFO described as the UK's first trial of bank executives for conduct during the 2008 financial crisis. John Varley had been acquitted earlier after the trial judge ruled the evidence against him insufficient and the Court of Appeal dismissed the SFO's appeal on 21 June 2019.
facts.quote: the Court of Appeal dismissed that appeal on 21 June 2019. Mr Varley was therefore acquitted on both counts.

facts.claim: On 25 November 2024 the FCA fined Barclays £40 million in total (£30 million on Barclays plc and £10 million on Barclays Bank plc) for failing to disclose certain arrangements with Qatari entities in 2008, finding the failure reckless and lacking integrity. The FCA had first issued warning notices in 2013, paused its case during the SFO proceedings, proposed £50 million in 2022 decision notices, and finalised the lower figure after Barclays withdrew its Upper Tribunal referral on 22 November 2024. Barclays said it did not accept the findings.
facts.quote: a financial penalty of £30 million on Barclays plc and a financial penalty of £10 million on Barclays Bank plc

sources.title: FCA publishes Decision Notices for Barclays plc and Barclays Bank plc

facts.claim: The FCA's final notices state that in the 2008 capital raising the Qatari entities were to be paid an additional fee of 1.75% of their maximum commitment, amounting to just over £40 million, which Barclays did not disclose; the FCA alleged the bank agreed to pay £322 million to the Qataris for advisory services.
facts.quote: the Qatari entities would be paid an additional fee of 1.75% of their maximum commitment in the capital raising (a figure amounting to just over £40 million)

sources.title: UK watchdog fines Barclays $55m over fees paid to Qatari entities

facts.claim: The FCA later found, in an Upper Tribunal ruling, that former Barclays executive Thomas Kalaris was dishonest in two FCA enforcement interviews about events during his time at Barclays and was therefore not fit to be a senior manager at a regulated business.
facts.quote: Mr Kalaris was dishonest in 2 enforcement interviews the FCA conducted into events that occurred during his time at Barclays

sources.title: Upper Tribunal ruling on Thomas Llewellyn Kalaris

connections.claim: Barclays raised capital from Qatar Holding LLC in June and October 2008 and lent it $3 billion in November 2008; the SFO charged Barclays Bank PLC over the loan and the FCA fined Barclays in 2024 for not disclosing fees paid to the Qatari entities.
connections.quote: a US$3 billion loan given to Qatar Holding LLC between 1 October and 30 November 2008

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): 'BlackRock leveraged this position to acquire Barclays Global Investors (BGI/iShares) in 2009 for pennies on the dollar' — the 2009 BGI sale is documented in the barclays-global-investors file from Barclays' SEC filings (about $13.5 billion at announcement, $15.2 billion at completion); no source opened supports 'pennies on the dollar', and the BGI sale was not re-researched here because the web search budget was exhausted.
Whether Qatar Holding LLC is a subsidiary of the Qatar Investment Authority was not confirmed from the SFO or FCA pages opened; the connection is recorded as 'other' on that basis.
The date of the Upper Tribunal ruling on Thomas Kalaris was not shown in the FCA statement snippet.
The exact May 2018 Crown Court dismissal date and the High Court decision date (reported as October 2018) should be confirmed on the SFO case page.
